title: Supported cohomology as morphisms
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions].
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a
closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], with complementary
open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion].
Work on the small pro-etale
sites with constant coefficient sheaves $A_T$ and ambient derived categories
$D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $i_*$ be
the underived module direct image [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image].
For any bounded-below complex $F$ of $A_X$-module sheaves and every integer
$a$, there is an isomorphism, natural in $F$,
$$
H^a_Z(X,F)\;\cong\;
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)}(i_*A_Z,F[a]),
$$
where the left side is the cohomology of derived supported sections
[def-pur-support-cohomology] and $i_*A_Z$ is placed in degree zero.
The shift uses the cochain convention $(F[a])^r=F^{r+a}$
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. No constructibility or finite-Tor
condition is imposed on $F$.

proof.text: First identify the sections of the coefficient sheaf on every scheme $T$. Degree-zero comparison [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison], with the constant-ring identification [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], identifies $A_T(T)$ on the pro-etale site with the sections of the constant etale coefficient sheaf. The underlying set of a constant ring sheaf is the constant set sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-underlying-sets]; the same sheafification of the constant additive group identifies its additive structure. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant] gives $A_T(T)=\operatorname{LC}(|T|,A)$. Addition and multiplication are pointwise: on the open fibres both sections are constant and their operations are the operations of $A$. Pullback along a scheme morphism sends a function to its composite with the underlying continuous map: restrict to the open fibres, where the section is the indicated constant and the comparison maps preserve that constant, then glue. For a weakly etale $W\to X$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $A_X(W)$ with $A_W(W)$, and also identifies $A_Z(W\times_XZ)$ with $A_{W\times_XZ}(W\times_XZ)$. These identifications therefore describe restrictions as restrictions of locally constant functions.

source.place: Proof: coefficient unit; its sections described explicitly before the supported-Hom calculation

proof.text: Put $P=i_*A_Z$ and let $\rho:A_X\to P$ be the constant-coefficient structure map. By [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] and step 1, its component at $W\to X$ restricts locally constant functions from $|W|$ to the closed subspace $|W_Z|$, where $W_Z=W\times_XZ$. The projection $W_Z\to W$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], so its underlying space is indeed the closed subspace used here. It is locally surjective. Indeed, given $s:|W_Z|\to A$ locally constant and $z\in|W_Z|$, choose an open neighbourhood $V_z\subset W$ whose intersection with $W_Z$ lies in the fibre of $s(z)$; the constant section $s(z)$ on $V_z$ lifts $s$ there. On $W\setminus W_Z$ the target section is zero and lifts to zero. These opens cover $W$. This Zariski cover is a pro-etale cover by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each affine open $B\subset W$, choose affine open neighbourhoods of its points contained in intersections of $B$ with members of the displayed cover; these exist since schemes are locally affine. Quasi-compactness of $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] selects finitely many of these affine neighbourhoods covering $B$, exactly as required in the covering definition. The local-surjectivity criterion [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] makes the underlying abelian map epic; it is also epic among module sheaves since equality of module maps is equality of their underlying maps. This proves that $\rho$ is epic without imposing quasi-compactness on $j$.

source.place: Proof: supported sections and the coefficient unit; local lifting for the closed coefficient sheaf written out

proof.text: By [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], $j_!A_U$ is the sheafification of the extension presheaf [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Construct $\epsilon:j_!A_U\to A_X$ as follows. By clause (4) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], an object $W$ has at most one map to $U$. When it has one, send its extension-presheaf section to the same section of $A_X(W)$ under the coefficient identification of clause (2); otherwise use the zero map from the zero presheaf value. These maps are module-linear and commute with restrictions by the presheaf restriction formula, including the case of an arrow from an object mapping to $U$ to an object not mapping to $U$, where the source restriction starts at zero. The universal property of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives $\epsilon$. The composite $\rho\epsilon$ is zero: on every nonzero presheaf summand $W\to U$ one has $W_Z=\varnothing$ and $P(W)=0$, so the composite is zero before sheafification and hence after it by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Conversely, for $f\in\ker(\rho_W)$, step 1 makes $f$ a locally constant function vanishing on $W_Z$. Its nonzero locus $O\subset W$ is open and closed and lies in $W\times_XU$. On $O$ the section $f|_O$ supplies a section of the extension presheaf and thus of $j_!A_U$; on $W\setminus O$ take zero. They agree on the empty overlap and glue to a section of $j_!A_U(W)$ mapping to $f$. Thus $\operatorname{im}(\epsilon)=\ker(\rho)$. Together with the epimorphism of step 2 this proves that $P$ is the cokernel of $\epsilon$ in the abelian category of module sheaves.

source.place: Proof: supported sections and the coefficient unit; the constant-sheaf cokernel calculation replaces the unrestricted support-comparison assertion

proof.text: The cokernel universal property from step 3 gives $\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)=\ker(\operatorname{Hom}(A_X,M)\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A_U,M))$. For any module sheaf $N$ over a constant coefficient ring, evaluation on $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(A_T,N)$ with $N(T)$: the inverse sends $s\in N(T)$ to the map $a\mapsto a\,s|_V$ on each site object $V$. These are inverse module maps and commute with restrictions by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Compute the other Hom group explicitly. By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], a map $\beta:j_!A_U\to M$ is uniquely a module-presheaf map from the extension presheaf of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] to $M$. The site and coefficient identifications of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] give $\beta\mapsto\beta_U(1)\in M(U)$, where $1$ is taken in the unique $U\to U$ summand before sheafification. Conversely, for $s\in M(U)$, on an object $V$ mapping to $U$ send $a\in A_U(V)=A_X(V)$ to $a\,s|_V$; on an object not mapping to $U$ use the zero map from the zero presheaf value. These maps commute with restrictions: when $V$ maps to $U$, semilinearity gives $(a\,s|_V)|_{V'}=a|_{V'}\,s|_{V'}$; otherwise the source value is zero, including when $V'$ maps to $U$. Sheafification gives the required map $\beta$. Evaluation returns $s$, and conversely naturality along $V\to U$ gives $\beta_V(1)=\beta_U(1)|_V$, so linearity recovers $\beta_V(a)=a\,\beta_U(1)|_V$ on every summand. Thus these constructions are inverse additive identifications $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!A_U,M)\cong M(U)$. Under them precomposition with the explicitly constructed $\epsilon$ is restriction $M(X)\to M(U)$, since its $U$-summand sends $1$ to $1$. Hence the displayed kernel is $\ker(M(X)\to M(U))=\Gamma_Z(X,M)$ by [def-pur-support-cohomology]. We obtain an additive natural isomorphism $v(M):=\operatorname{Hom}(P,M)\cong\Gamma_Z(X,M)$. Naturality holds because a module map $M\to N$ applies its section map to the same supported section on both sides.

source.place: Proof: global sections are Hom from the coefficient unit; restriction and naturality written out

proof.text: Use the chosen small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and the module universe specified by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Thus the small-site hypothesis of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] holds, and the category $\mathcal A$ of all $A_X$-module sheaves is Grothendieck. It has enough injectives: apply the termwise monic resolution of [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to $M[0]$; its degree-zero component embeds each $M$ into an injective object. Put $w=\Gamma_Z(X,-)$ and let $\theta:v\xrightarrow{\sim}w$ be the additive natural isomorphism of step 4. Applying $\theta$ termwise gives an isomorphism of functors on bounded-below homotopy categories: its compatibility with each differential and with homotopies is the naturality of $\theta$ and its additivity. The universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] derives this isomorphism without an additional geometric hypothesis. Explicitly, let $\alpha_v:QK(v)\to RvQ$ and $\alpha_w:QK(w)\to RwQ$ be the derived units. Apply clause (1) to $\alpha_w\circ QK(\theta)$ to obtain $\gamma:Rv\to Rw$, and to $\alpha_v\circ QK(\theta^{-1})$ to obtain $\delta:Rw\to Rv$. Their composites satisfy $(\delta\gamma)Q\circ\alpha_v=\alpha_v$ and $(\gamma\delta)Q\circ\alpha_w=\alpha_w$, since $\theta^{-1}\theta$ and $\theta\theta^{-1}$ are identities. The uniqueness in clause (1) forces both composites to be identities. By [def-pur-support-cohomology], $Rw=R\Gamma_Z(X,-)$, so degree-$a$ cohomology gives $H_Z^a(X,F)\cong H^a(Rv(F))$, naturally in $F$.

source.place: Proof: derive the natural supported-sections/Hom identity in the ambient module-sheaf category

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-p1-rhom-hom-derived-roof] to the abelian category $\mathcal A$ from step 5, the object $M=P=i_*A_Z$, the bounded-below object $F$, and $n=a$. Its statement gives $H^a(Rv(F))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(P[0],F[a])$, natural in $F$, with no condition on $P$ being projective or locally free. Concretely a cocycle $f:P\to I^a$ becomes the complex map $P[0]\to I[a]$ and then is composed with the inverse of the shifted resolution isomorphism $F[a]\to I[a]$. A boundary $d_I^{a-1}h$ gives the homotopy with sole component $(-1)^a h:P\to I^{a-1}$ for the shifted differential, so the formula respects cohomology classes. Compose with step 5. This is the displayed identification with the underived $i_*A_Z$ in degree zero, and proves naturality for every integer $a$.

Converts the explicit local constant lifts into a sheaf epimorphism.

Generic Grothendieck property of the ambient module-sheaf category.
